craft_notes: Sthāyin: everywhere-body (knowledge-everywhere, body-everywhere, none-else-seeing: the triple-everything then vanishing self: the paradox is the FORM: everywhere AND vanished). Rows: row 2 (vanishing→form casteless). Close: unsurpassed (anuttama — the top-word: after vanishing, UNSURPASSED: the irony held without comment). Rejected: 'omniscient' doctrine — killed: everywhere knowledge kept (the distributive, not the claim); 'formless' — NO: form kept (he has form, casteless: form-casteless kept together).

lines: Everywhere knowledge, everywhere body, seeing none else:
vanishing self — of Him form, casteless, unsurpassed.
l4.sanskrit_cite: bhayā sarvaṃ ravayati sarvado vyāpako 'khile | iti bhairavaśabdasya santatoccāraṇāc chivaḥ

reads_against.argmap: How does Śiva come from the word? → Constant uttering of the Bhairava-word makes Śiva from all resounding.
c1_essence: Fear resounds all in wholeness: Bhairava's word, Śiva.
reads_against.c1_rasa: vīra with śānta undertow (resolve laid quiet)
